A Division Bench of Justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Achal Sachdev added that every time bureaucrats and those in the police ignore their oath and allegiance to India and its Constitution, people would view them as an oppressive vestige of the British Empire. Such a situation will arouse angst and hatred towards them and end up creating an environment of civil unrest in the State, the Bench added. It warned that if the Court fails to act against excesses of bureaucrats, the State may be reduced to an Orwellian Dystopia. "This Court, while correcting their excesses and/or illegalities, especially those that impinge upon the civil liberties of the citizens without adequate cause or due process (inhering in the procedure established by law), may pass harsh orders to compensate the citizen so wronged, besides recording their despotic conduct. items.title: 7 dead, officials suspended: What happened after the Satya Niketan building collapse?
items.summary: A five-storey building collapsed in Delhi’s Satya Niketan on Sunday afternoon. So far, 12 people have been pulled out from the debris, with seven deaths confirmed. Following the incident, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi has suspended its deputy commissioner, executive engineer, superintendent engineer, assistant engineer and junior engineer. Satya Niketan is home to a large number of Delhi University students, many of whom are forced to live in rented accommodation after failing to secure hostel rooms at their colleges. A local resident, Varun, said, “The entire building collapsed in one go. I think around 40 people could be trapped under the debris. Some repair work was going on here.” Police have registered a case and launched an investigation. The Delhi Fire Services said it received information about the collapse shortly after 1.30 pm. What led to the collapse? And what has happened since? Watch. Our new project visits the landscape described in Vande Mataram as it stands today, to ask what has become of the country the national song sings about. Support it here .

The case is likely to be taken up for hearing by Judge Mridul Gupta on Tuesday. Joshi was questioned for nearly nine hours by the Delhi Police Special Cell on September 2 in connection with a case registered against him over his social media activity. Joshi is a retired 1992-batch Indian Posts and Telecommunications Accounts and Finance Service officer who retired as an Additional Secretary-rank official in March 2026. He was allegedly picked up while on a morning walk and taken to the Counter Intelligence unit’s office in New Friends Colony. Police said he was questioned in connection with an FIR registered two days earlier and was released after his statement was recorded. The plea by Joshi has been filed through advocates Aadil Singh Boparai, Ronit Bose and Nikunj Bindal.

items.title: Supreme Court directs Centre, States to set up 449 exclusive NDPS courts within 6 months
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday directed the Central government, States, and Union Territories to take immediate steps to establish 449 exclusive courts for trial of cases under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act (NDPS Act). A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana issued the directive after taking on record a status report filed by the Union of India, which revealed that only 176 of the required 449 exclusive NDPS courts are presently operational across the country. The Court expressed concern over the alarming surge in narcotics cases nationwide and directed setting up 449 courts, preferably within six months. “Having regard to the current pendency of cases under the NDPS Act and the alarming increase in offences under the Act across the country, it is expedient and in the interest of justice that the requisite 449 exclusive NDPS courts be established at the earliest,” the Court recorded. The bench directed all States and Union Territories to urgently arrange the necessary court infrastructure and appoint judicial and administrative staff to bridge the deficit. items.title: Kochi filmmaker is only Indian to be selected to Artists Academy, New York Film Festival
items.summary: In the list of roles Raymond George Dias has played in his young life – filmmaker, photographer, and multidisciplinary artist, with a background in law – you might look for the word ‘poet’, if you have come across one or many of his works. His words and visuals tend to carry the hangover of a poem, lyrical and musical pieces hopping through time and space. All that art has paved the way for his selection in the Film at Lincoln Center (FLC) Artists Academy 2026, held as part of the New York Film Festival. He is one of the 12 filmmakers from around the world to participate in the programme, to be held between September 25 and October 12. The FLC Academies support the next generation of film artists and critics by conducting a workshop, during which participants can meet with established filmmakers and others, and find new opportunities. The FLC page describes Raymond’s approach to art as a “spiritual rite, a pilgrimage of unmaking and becoming”. “I am the only filmmaker selected from India.
